HOME SCHOOLING

By: Jo Munnik | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
THE STATE AND COST OF EDUCATION IN SOUTH AFRICA HAS MANY PARENTS TURNING TO HOME SCHOOLING. IS HOME SCHOOLING A BETTER OPTION THAN TRADITIONAL SCHOOLING?

Summary:
PARENTS IN SOUTH AFRICA ARE INCREASINGLY TURNING TO HOME SCHOOLING FOR VARIOUS REASONS - THE QUALITY OF EDUCATION IN SOUTH AFRICA, DIFFICULTIES GETTING INTO SCHOOLS, BULLYING AND THE COST OF GOOD EDUCATION.

WE SPEAK TO TWO FAMILIES ABOUT THEIR PERSONAL HOME SCHOOLING EXPERIENCES - ONE WITH A CHILD WHO HAS COMPLETED MATRIC AND CONSEQUENTLY, THEY PUT THEIR SECOND CHILD INTO A TRADITIONAL SCHOOL. AND A FAMILY WITH TWO CHILDREN WHO ARE CURRENTLY AT PRIMARY SCHOOL LEVEL AND ARE VERY HAPPY WITH HOME SCHOOLING.

THEY TELL US THEIR STORIES AND EXPERIENCES WITH HOME SCHOOLING AS WELL THEIR REASONS FOR OPTING FOR HOME SCHOOLING INSTEAD OF TRADITIONAL SCHOOLING.

EXPERTS INCLUDE - THE HOME SCHOOLING ASSOCIATION, THE PETZALOZZI TRUST ( AN ADVOCACY GROUP / LEGAL SERVICE FOR HOME SCHOOLERS), THE DEPT OF EDUCATION AND AN EXPERT IN EDUCATION.

Press Release:


Home Schooling
Over 60 000 South African learners do not attend formal schooling. Their parents have opted to take their education into their own hands and school them at home. But, from primary to high school, is this increasingly popular trend a viable alternative to traditional forms of education? Carte Blanche weighs up the pros and cons of home schooling.


Script:


CECILE:
I ACTUALLY USED TO LOOK AT PEOPLE WHO HOME SCHOOLED AND THOUGHT THEY WERE VERY BRAVE. NOT SOMETHING I COULD EVER DO.

VAL COMMENT:
THIS IS JUST A LITTLE BIT MORE UNUSUAL THAN THE MAJORITY FO SOCIETY DO IT. SO, IT WAS A BIG LEAP OF FAITH.

VO:
HOME SCHOOLING KICKED OFF IN SOUTH AFRICA IN THE NINETIES WITH A FEW THOUSAND PUPILS LEARNING IN THIS WAY. TODAY THERE ARE WELL OVER 60 000 YOUNG PEOPLE EDUCATED AT HOME.

DEREK LINK:
THIS USED TO BE THE GARAGE AT THE HOME OF VALERIA AND RUAN TALIAN, IT’S NOW THE CLASSROOM FOR THEIR TWO CHILDREN EMILY AND KYLE.

KYLE: WHAT’S A MOM AND A TEACHER MIXED UP. A MEACHER. SHE’S LIKE A MEACHER.
DEREK: AS A MEACHER IS IT DIFFICULT TO SEE HER AS A TEACHER AND A MOM.
KYLE: NO, NOT AT ALL.

VO: THE REASONS FOR PARENTS INCREASINGLY TURNING TO HOME SCHOOLING INCLUDE: LONG SCHOOL WAITING LISTS, THE POOR STANDARD OF EDUCATION, EXORBITANT FEES, RELIGIOUS PREFERENCES AND TO DEAL WITH MEDICAL OR REMEDIAL DIFFICULTIES.

DR SIMELANE:
IT IS THE RIGHT OF EVERY CHILD TO RECEIVE BASIC EDUCATION.

VO: ACCORDING TO DR MOSES SIMELANE, THE DEPARTMENT OF BASIC EDUCATION SUPPORTS HOME SCHOOLING.

DR SIMELANE:
THE DEPARTMENT HAS INCLUDED A SECTION IN THE SA SCHOOLS ACT WHICH PROVIDES FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF HOME EDUCATION SITES AND EDUCATION OF CHILDREN IN THEIR HOMES HOME.

VO: VALERIA IS A QUALIFIED PRE-PRIMARY SCHOOL TEACHER. SHE TOOK HER SON KYLE OUT OF A TRADITIONAL SCHOOL AT THE END OF GRADE 1.

VALERIA
THE OVER CROWDING FOR ME IS HUGE AND A LOT OF KIDS GET LOST IN TRANSLATION LIKE THAT. NOT ENOUGH EMOTIONAL SUPPORT I THINK FOR THE CHILDREN.

VO: CECILE LEWIS EDUCATED BOTH OF HER CHILDREN AT HOME. When her son James was four, she realized that he WAS AHEAD OF HIS PEERS. GIVEN THAT THEY LIVED IN A RURAL AREA, HER SCHOOLING OPTIONS WERE LIMITED.

CECILE
I WAS FACED WITH A CHILD WHO NEEDED STIMULATION, I REALISED THAT THE RESPONSIBILITY LAY ON MY SHOULDERS TO DO SOMETHING. AFTER ABOUT A YEAR I REALISED THERE WERE BENEFITS I WASN’T EXPECTING TO SEE.

VO: THERE IS A WIDE VARIETY OF HOME SCHOOL CURRICULUMS FROM WHICH TO CHOOSE. LOCAL AND INTERNATIONAL OPTIONS VARY IN QUALITY AND COST SO IT IS IMPORTANT TO DO YOUR HOMEWORK BEFORE COMMITTING TO A SYLLABUS.

DEREK LINK
THE LEWIS FAMILY EDUCATED BOTH THEIR CHILDREN AT HOME. BUT DID EXPERIENCE SOME CHALLENGES AT A HIGH SCHOOL LEVEL.

CECILE
SENIOR SCHOOL IT’S A DIFFERENT KETTLE OF FISH. ESPECIALLY FROM GRADE 9 UP. VERY STRESSFUL ON THE HOUSEHOLD. I HAD SLEEPLESS NIGHTS. YOU GET TO GRADE 10 UP - SCIENCE, CHEMISTRY AND THEN TO ADD TO THAT YOU DON’T HAVE A LABORATORY IN YOUR HOUSE. HOW DO YOU COPE?

JAMES
YOU ARE AT A DISTINCT DISADVANTAGE WHEN YOU DON’T HAVE FORMALLY TUITION. LECTURES OR TEACHERS TO ASK, ESPECIALLY WHEN YOU MOVE INTO THOSE HIGHER LEVELS AND YOUR PARENTS CAN NO LONGER HELP YOU.
.
BRAHM COMMENT
HOW MANY PARENTS ARE ABLE TO TEACH HIGH SCHOOL ENGLISH AND MATHEMATICS AND SCIENCE AND FRENCH?

VO: PROFESSOR BRAHM FLEISCH SAYS THE CHOICE TO HOME SCHOOL CAN’T BE UNDERESTIMATED.


BRAHM
THERE IS A GREAT CHALLENGE AND IT REQUIRES RELATIVELY SPECIALIZED KNOWLEDGE TO PROVIDE A COMPREHENSIVE AND SOUND EDUCATION THAT MEETS THE STANDARD OF OUR GRADE 12 EXAMS.

VO: EMILY AND KYLE ARE FOLLOWING A LOCAL CURRICULUM CALLED THEO-CENTRIC EDUCATION.

(MOMENT – KYLE & CECILE)

VO: CECILE’S SON, JAMES, OPTED FOR THE BRITISH CAMBRIDGE SYLLABUS INSTEAD OF A LOCAL MATRIC EQUIVALENT.

DEREK LINK:
JAMES FEELS THAT COMING FROM A HOME SCHOOL PUT HIM AT A DISADVANTAGE WHEN APPLYING TO STUDY MEDICINE AT UNIVERSITY.

CECILE
WE THOUGHT INITIALLY, MAYBE IN IGNORANCE, A CAMBRIDGE LETTERHEAD SIGNED BY THE VICE CHANCELLOR WOULD BE ENOUGH. BUT THERE WAS A LOT THAT COUNTED AGAINST HIM. HE WAS VERY FRUSTRATED WHEN HE FILLED IN HIS UNIVERSITY FORMS. THERE WAS A LOT OF BOXES ON THE FORM THAT JAMES COULD NOT TICK.

JAMES
IF I HAD TO DO IT AGAIN, KNOWING I WOULD HAVE WANTED TO GO INTO MEDICINE, I WOULD HAVE GONE TO FORMAL SCHOOL, HAD THE OPPORTUNITIES TO BECOME A PREFECT, FIRST STRING SPORT OF SOME SORT.

VO: JAMES’S YOUNGER SISTER KAYLEIGH WANTS TO STUDY VETERINARY SCIENCE. CONSEQUENTLY, CECILE HAS MOVED HER FROM HOME SCHOOLING INTO THE LOCAL MAIN STREAM SCHOOL.

DEREK
HOW DID SHE HANDLE THAT TRANSITION?

CECILE:
SHE COPED VERY WELL WITH THE SOCIAL. THE PART SHE COULDN’T UNDERSTAND THIS BUSINESS OF LESSONS, AND YOU WALK FROM ONE CLASS TO THE NEXT AND YOU GET DISTRACTED HERE– SHE BATTLED, FELT HER TIME WAS BEING WASTED.

DEREK
IF YOU COULD DO IT ALL OVER AGAIN, WHAT WOULD YOU CHANGE ABOUT HOME SCHOOLING?

CECILE
I WOULD DEFINITELY DO JUNIOR SCHOOL. WITHOUT A DOUBT. MAINLY BECAUSE OF THE BENEFITS I SAW UNFOLDING IN FRONT OF MY EYES AS WE WALKED THAT ROAD.
SENIOR SCHOOL, I WOULDN’T ATTEMPT IT.

DEREK
HOME SCHOOLING IS NOT A DECISION TO BE TAKEN LIGHTLY. AND I’M NOT JUST TALKING ABOUT THE EFFECT ON THE CHILDREN’S EDUCATION.

DEREK
VALERIA, AS A MOTHER TURNED TEACHER DO YOU HAVE TO GIVE UP WORK. IS THAT IT?

VALERIA
I HAVE READ OF PEOPLE WORKING AND TEACHING. PERSONALLY FOR ME IT IS NOT AN OPTION.

VO: HOME SCHOOLING COSTS BETWEEN R 400 AND R 2000 A MONTH. MOST PARENTS CHOOSING THIS OPTION RUN SINGLE INCOME HOUSEHOLDS.

VALERIA
YOU DO NOT NEED TO BE A QUALIFIED PROFESSOR OR TEACHER TO TEACH YOUR CHILDREN. BUT YOU DO NEED TO BE COMMITTED TO THE CAUSE.

BRAHM
PARENTS ARE THE FIRST AND MOST IMPORTANT TEACHERS. CAN THEY PROVIDE THE COMPLEX LEARNING THAT TAKES PLACE IN SCHOOLS? I THINK THERE ARE MANY CASES WHERE HOME SCHOOLING DOESN’T NECESSARILY GIVE THEM THE VARIETY OF LEARNING EXPERIENCES THAT CHILDREN NEED.

VO: HOWEVER, PARENTS DO NOT HAVE TO DO IT ALL ON THEIR OWN.

DR MOSES SIMELANE:
THE POLICY ALLOWS FOR A PARENT TO ENLIST SERVICES OF A TUTOR, IN CASE THE PARENT CANNOT PROVIDE THE ACTUAL TEACHING.

VO: FOR VALERIA HOME SCHOOLING PROVIDES A PLATFORM TO GIVE HER CHILDREN AN EDUCATION WITHOUT LIMITS.

VALERIA:
IT’S UP TO US AS PARENTS TO PROVIDE OUR CHILDREN WITH ANYTHING THAT SPARKS THEIR INTEREST AND AT SCHOOL THERE ISN’T TIME FOR THAT.

VO: EMILY AND KYLE BOTH HAVE AN ARTISTIC FLAIR. SO, VALERIA HAS TAILOR MADE THEIR TIMETABLE TO ACCOMMODATE A FULL DAY OF ART EVERY FRIDAY.

DEREK : DO YOU THINK YOU ARE LEARNING MORE HERE THAN AT SCHOOL?
KYLE: VERY MUCH MORE THAN SCHOOLS.
DEREK : REALLY.
KYLE: YIP.

VO: DESPITE THE DIFFICULTIES HE FACED IN LATER YEARS, JAMES IS FOR HOME SCHOOLING AT A JUNIOR SCHOOL LEVEL.

JAMES
I LEARNT HOW TO RESEARCH ON MY OWN AT A VERY YOUNG AGE. I LEARNT A THIRST FOR KNOWLEDGE AT A VERY YOUNG AGE. I DID NOT RESENT WORK AT ANY POINT THROUGHOUT MY LIFE. WHERE I THINK HOMEWORK AND PROJECTS CAN PREVENT CHILDREN FROM FINDING A LOVE FOR KNOWLEDGE AND LEARNING.

DEREK
ARE YOU IN THIS FOR THE LONG HAUL? MATRIC CAN BE DAUNTING FOR PARENTS.

VALERIA
YES I DO THINK SO. AND I DO THINK WE ARE GOING TO HAVE TO GET SOME EXTERNAL HELP AT SOME POINT. I WOULD LIKE TO FOLLOW THROUGH WITH THIS ALL THE WAY TO MATRIC AND HOPEFULLY THEY WOULD TOO.

VO: STUDENTS CHOOSING TO DO MATRIC THROUGH HOME SCHOOLING MUST REGISTER WITH ONE OF SEVERAL INDEPENDENT EXAMINATION BOARDS EITHER THROUGH THEIR CURRICULUM COORDINATORS OR INDEPENDENTLY.

DEREK
BRAHM, WHAT ELEMENTS WOULD YOU SAY IS MISSING FROM EDUCATION?




BRAHM
THE ELEMENT OF SOCIALISATION. ONE OF THE THINGS THAT CHILDREN LEARN IN SCHOOLS IS HOW TO GET ON WITH OTHER CHILDREN, HOW TO SHARE.

JAMES
I WILL TELL YOU OUT OF EXPERIENCE THAT IT DOESN’T HAPPEN NATURALLY. YOU HAVE TO GO OUT OF YOUR WAY TO FORM THESE SORTS OF INTERACTIONS FOR YOUR CHILD.

VALERIA
IT HAS BECOME A LIFESTYLE TO FIND ACTIVITIES FOR THE CHILDREN TO DO TO MEET OTHER CHILDREN.

DEREK: HOW DO YOU MEET THEM?
EMILY: SAY HELLO.
(DEREK LAUGHS)

VO: THE SOUTH AFRICAN SCHOOLS ACT SAYS THAT ALL CHILDREN BETWEEN THE AGES OF 6 AND 15 HAVE TO BE OFFICIALLY REGISTERED WITHIN A SCHOOLING ENVIRONMENT. BUT, WHEN IT COMES TO HOME SCHOOLING, REGISTRATION IS A BIT OF A GREY AREA.

DEREK
WHAT ABOUT THE LEGAL FRAMEWORK IN THIS COUNTRY, THE LAWS WITH EDUCATION, HOW DO THEY AFFECT YOU?

VALERIA
WE DON’T KNOW WHERE WE STAND. I FIND IT ALL A LITTLE CONFUSING.

VO:
OVER 90% OF HOME SCHOOLS ARE NOT REGISTERED WITH THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION.

BRAHM
WE KNOW VERY LITTLE ABOUT THE STANDARD OF HOME SCHOOLING ACROSS THE SOUTH AFRICAN CONTEXT. PARTICULARLY HOME SCHOOLING THAT IS NOT REGISTERED. WE ARE NOT ABLE TO SAY WITH ANY CERTAINTY WHAT IS ACTUALLY GOING ON. PART OF THE REASON WE REQUIRE REGISTRATION IS TO ENSURE AT LEAST A PLAN IS IN PLACE.


DR MOSES SIMELANE
MAYBE AS A DEPARTMENT WE HAVE NOT QUITE ADVOCATED FOR THE POLICY, THE 1999 POLICY ON HOME EDUCATION, WHICH PROVIDES PARENTS WITH GUIDANCE IN TERMS OF HOW THEY GO ABOUT REGISTERING WITH THE DEPARTMENT. THESE ARE ISSUES THAT ARE ALL UNDER REVIEW, WHICH WE WANT TO OUT INTO POLICY AND TRY AND REGULATE.

BRAHM
I THINK THAT PARENTS THAT WANT TO DO HOME SCHOOLING, THINK VERY CAREFULLY ABOUT IT. .. AFTER THEY HAVE BEEN THROUGH THE PROCESSES AND THEY CARE CONVINCED THAT IS IN THE BEST INTEREST OF THEIR CHILDREN, THEN CERTAINLY THEY SHOULD BE GOING AHEAD.

CECILE
IF YOU HAVE STRONG CONVICTIONS AND YOU BELIEVE YOU CAN DO A BETTER JOB THAN THE SCHOOL UP THE ROAD THEN GO FOR YOUR BADGE.

PROMOS:

15”
VO: HOME SCHOOLING IS BECOMING A POPULAR CHOICE,
WITH OVER 60 000 SOUTH AFRICAN LEARNERS BEING EDUCATED IN THIS WAY.

SOUND UP – JAMES:
I LEARNT A THIRST FOR KNOWLEDGE AT A VERY YOUNG AGE, I DIDN’T RESENT WORK.
VO: WE WEIGH UP THE PROS AND CONS OF HOME SCHOOLING.

15”

CECILE SOUND UP: I WAS FACED WITH A CHILD WHO NEEDED STIMULATION, AND I REALISED THAT THE RESPONSIBILITY LAY ON MY SHOULDERS TO DO SOMETHING WITH IT.
VO: PARENTS ARE INCREASINGLY TAKING EDUCATION INTO THEIR OWN HANDS AND OPTING FOR HOME SCHOOLING. BUT, IS IT A VIABLE ALTERNATIVE?





10”

VO: WOULD YOU TAKE THE LEAP INTO HOME SCHOOLING?
CECILE: IF YOU HAVE STRONG CONVICTIONS AND YOU BELIEVE YOU CAN DO A BETTER JOB THAN THE SCHOOL UP THE ROAD THEN GO FOR YOUR BADGE.

DEREK HOW DID SHE HANDLE THAT TRANSITION? CECILE: SHE COPED VERY WELL WITH THE SOCIAL. THE PART SHE COULDN’T UNDERSTAND THIS BUSINESS OF LESSONS, AND YOU WALK FROM ONE CLASS TO THE NEXT AND YOU GET DISTRACTED HERE– SHE BATTLED, FELT HER TIME WAS BEING WASTED. DEREK IF YOU COULD DO IT ALL OVER AGAIN, WHAT WOULD YOU CHANGE ABOUT HOME SCHOOLING? CECILE I WOULD DEFINITELY DO JUNIOR SCHOOL. WITHOUT A DOUBT. MAINLY BECAUSE OF THE BENEFITS I SAW UNFOLDING IN FRONT OF MY EYES AS WE WALKED THAT ROAD. SENIOR SCHOOL, I WOULDN’T ATTEMPT IT. DEREK HOME SCHOOLING IS NOT A DECISION TO BE TAKEN LIGHTLY. AND I’M NOT JUST TALKING ABOUT THE EFFECT ON THE CHILDREN’S EDUCATION. DEREK VALERIA, AS A MOTHER TURNED TEACHER DO YOU HAVE TO GIVE UP WORK. IS THAT IT? VALERIA I HAVE READ OF PEOPLE WORKING AND TEACHING. PERSONALLY FOR ME IT IS NOT AN OPTION. VO: HOME SCHOOLING COSTS BETWEEN R 400 AND R 2000 A MONTH. MOST PARENTS CHOOSING THIS OPTION RUN SINGLE INCOME HOUSEHOLDS. VALERIA YOU DO NOT NEED TO BE A QUALIFIED PROFESSOR OR TEACHER TO TEACH YOUR CHILDREN. BUT YOU DO NEED TO BE COMMITTED TO THE CAUSE. BRAHM PARENTS ARE THE FIRST AND MOST IMPORTANT TEACHERS. CAN THEY PROVIDE THE COMPLEX LEARNING THAT TAKES PLACE IN SCHOOLS? I THINK THERE ARE MANY CASES WHERE HOME SCHOOLING DOESN’T NECESSARILY GIVE THEM THE VARIETY OF LEARNING EXPERIENCES THAT CHILDREN NEED. VO: HOWEVER, PARENTS DO NOT HAVE TO DO IT ALL ON THEIR OWN. DR MOSES SIMELANE: THE POLICY ALLOWS FOR A PARENT TO ENLIST SERVICES OF A TUTOR, IN CASE THE PARENT CANNOT PROVIDE THE ACTUAL TEACHING. VO: FOR VALERIA HOME SCHOOLING PROVIDES A PLATFORM TO GIVE HER CHILDREN AN EDUCATION WITHOUT LIMITS. VALERIA: IT’S UP TO US AS PARENTS TO PROVIDE OUR CHILDREN WITH ANYTHING THAT SPARKS THEIR INTEREST AND AT SCHOOL THERE ISN’T TIME FOR THAT. VO: EMILY AND KYLE BOTH HAVE AN ARTISTIC FLAIR. SO, VALERIA HAS TAILOR MADE THEIR TIMETABLE TO ACCOMMODATE A FULL DAY OF ART EVERY FRIDAY. DEREK : DO YOU THINK YOU ARE LEARNING MORE HERE THAN AT SCHOOL? KYLE: VERY MUCH MORE THAN SCHOOLS. DEREK : REALLY. KYLE: YIP. VO: DESPITE THE DIFFICULTIES HE FACED IN LATER YEARS, JAMES IS FOR HOME SCHOOLING AT A JUNIOR SCHOOL LEVEL. JAMES I LEARNT HOW TO RESEARCH ON MY OWN AT A VERY YOUNG AGE. I LEARNT A THIRST FOR KNOWLEDGE AT A VERY YOUNG AGE. I DID NOT RESENT WORK AT ANY POINT THROUGHOUT MY LIFE. WHERE I THINK HOMEWORK AND PROJECTS CAN PREVENT CHILDREN FROM FINDING A LOVE FOR KNOWLEDGE AND LEARNING. DEREK ARE YOU IN THIS FOR THE LONG HAUL? MATRIC CAN BE DAUNTING FOR PARENTS. VALERIA YES I DO THINK SO. AND I DO THINK WE ARE GOING TO HAVE TO GET SOME EXTERNAL HELP AT SOME POINT. I WOULD LIKE TO FOLLOW THROUGH WITH THIS ALL THE WAY TO MATRIC AND HOPEFULLY THEY WOULD TOO. VO: STUDENTS CHOOSING TO DO MATRIC THROUGH HOME SCHOOLING MUST REGISTER WITH ONE OF SEVERAL INDEPENDENT EXAMINATION BOARDS EITHER THROUGH THEIR CURRICULUM COORDINATORS OR INDEPENDENTLY. DEREK BRAHM, WHAT ELEMENTS WOULD YOU SAY IS MISSING FROM EDUCATION? BRAHM THE ELEMENT OF SOCIALISATION. ONE OF THE THINGS THAT CHILDREN LEARN IN SCHOOLS IS HOW TO GET ON WITH OTHER CHILDREN, HOW TO SHARE. JAMES I WILL TELL YOU OUT OF EXPERIENCE THAT IT DOESN’T HAPPEN NATURALLY. YOU HAVE TO GO OUT OF YOUR WAY TO FORM THESE SORTS OF INTERACTIONS FOR YOUR CHILD. VALERIA IT HAS BECOME A LIFESTYLE TO FIND ACTIVITIES FOR THE CHILDREN TO DO TO MEET OTHER CHILDREN. DEREK: HOW DO YOU MEET THEM? EMILY: SAY HELLO. (DEREK LAUGHS) VO: THE SOUTH AFRICAN SCHOOLS ACT SAYS THAT ALL CHILDREN BETWEEN THE AGES OF 6 AND 15 HAVE TO BE OFFICIALLY REGISTERED WITHIN A SCHOOLING ENVIRONMENT. BUT, WHEN IT COMES TO HOME SCHOOLING, REGISTRATION IS A BIT OF A GREY AREA. DEREK WHAT ABOUT THE LEGAL FRAMEWORK IN THIS COUNTRY, THE LAWS WITH EDUCATION, HOW DO THEY AFFECT YOU? VALERIA WE DON’T KNOW WHERE WE STAND. I FIND IT ALL A LITTLE CONFUSING. VO: OVER 90% OF HOME SCHOOLS ARE NOT REGISTERED WITH THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION. BRAHM WE KNOW VERY LITTLE ABOUT THE STANDARD OF HOME SCHOOLING ACROSS THE SOUTH AFRICAN CONTEXT. PARTICULARLY HOME SCHOOLING THAT IS NOT REGISTERED. WE ARE NOT ABLE TO SAY WITH ANY CERTAINTY WHAT IS ACTUALLY GOING ON. PART OF THE REASON WE REQUIRE REGISTRATION IS TO ENSURE AT LEAST A PLAN IS IN PLACE. DR MOSES SIMELANE MAYBE AS A DEPARTMENT WE HAVE NOT QUITE ADVOCATED FOR THE POLICY, THE 1999 POLICY ON HOME EDUCATION, WHICH PROVIDES PARENTS WITH GUIDANCE IN TERMS OF HOW THEY GO ABOUT REGISTERING WITH THE DEPARTMENT. THESE ARE ISSUES THAT ARE ALL UNDER REVIEW, WHICH WE WANT TO OUT INTO POLICY AND TRY AND REGULATE. BRAHM I THINK THAT PARENTS THAT WANT TO DO HOME SCHOOLING, THINK VERY CAREFULLY ABOUT IT. .. AFTER THEY HAVE BEEN THROUGH THE PROCESSES AND THEY CARE CONVINCED THAT IS IN THE BEST INTEREST OF THEIR CHILDREN, THEN CERTAINLY THEY SHOULD BE GOING AHEAD. CECILE IF YOU HAVE STRONG CONVICTIONS AND YOU BELIEVE YOU CAN DO A BETTER JOB THAN THE SCHOOL UP THE ROAD THEN GO FOR YOUR BADGE. PROMOS: 15” VO: HOME SCHOOLING IS BECOMING A POPULAR CHOICE, WITH OVER 60 000 SOUTH AFRICAN LEARNERS BEING EDUCATED IN THIS WAY. SOUND UP – JAMES: I LEARNT A THIRST FOR KNOWLEDGE AT A VERY YOUNG AGE, I DIDN’T RESENT WORK. VO: WE WEIGH UP THE PROS AND CONS OF HOME SCHOOLING. 15” CECILE SOUND UP: I WAS FACED WITH A CHILD WHO NEEDED STIMULATION, AND I REALISED THAT THE RESPONSIBILITY LAY ON MY SHOULDERS TO DO SOMETHING WITH IT. VO: PARENTS ARE INCREASINGLY TAKING EDUCATION INTO THEIR OWN HANDS AND OPTING FOR HOME SCHOOLING. BUT, IS IT A VIABLE ALTERNATIVE? 10” VO: WOULD YOU TAKE THE LEAP INTO HOME SCHOOLING? CECILE: IF YOU HAVE STRONG CONVICTIONS AND YOU BELIEVE YOU CAN DO A BETTER JOB THAN THE SCHOOL UP THE ROAD THEN GO FOR YOUR BADGE.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): THE STATE AND COST OF EDUCATION IN SOUTH AFRICA HAS MANY PARENTS TURNING TO HOME SCHOOLING. IS HOME SCHOOLING A BETTER OPTION THAN TRADITIONAL SCHOOLING?
metadata.Summary: PARENTS IN SOUTH AFRICA ARE INCREASINGLY TURNING TO HOME SCHOOLING FOR VARIOUS REASONS - THE QUALITY OF EDUCATION IN SOUTH AFRICA, DIFFICULTIES GETTING INTO SCHOOLS, BULLYING AND THE COST OF GOOD EDUCATION. WE SPEAK TO TWO FAMILIES ABOUT THEIR PERSONAL HOME SCHOOLING EXPERIENCES - ONE WITH A CHILD WHO HAS COMPLETED MATRIC AND CONSEQUENTLY, THEY PUT THEIR SECOND CHILD INTO A TRADITIONAL SCHOOL. AND A FAMILY WITH TWO CHILDREN WHO ARE CURRENTLY AT PRIMARY SCHOOL LEVEL AND ARE VERY HAPPY WITH HOME SCHOOLING. THEY TELL US THEIR STORIES AND EXPERIENCES WITH HOME SCHOOLING AS WELL THEIR REASONS FOR OPTING FOR HOME SCHOOLING INSTEAD OF TRADITIONAL SCHOOLING. EXPERTS INCLUDE - THE HOME SCHOOLING ASSOCIATION, THE PETZALOZZI TRUST ( AN ADVOCACY GROUP / LEGAL SERVICE FOR HOME SCHOOLERS), THE DEPT OF EDUCATION AND AN EXPERT IN EDUCATION.
